text: Dron Blastbrew is a Wildhammer dwarf quest giver located at the Stormfeather Outpost in the Hinterlands.
Drunken Wingriders are Zandalari trolls found in Stormsea Landing on the Isle of Thunder. They are part of the Captain Halu'kal encounter.

Drizle is a furbolg quest giver located in Felwood. He is first seen with his companion Ferli trying to convince adventurers to gather honey from inside the Totem of Ruumbo. Later he tried to gather some more honey, but ends up being captured by the Deadwood tribe.
__NOTOC__ The Dripping Strider Egg drops from Lady Vashj in Serpentshrine Cavern.

Drov the Ruiner is found at the north end of the Valley of Destruction in Gronn Canyon in northwestern Gorgrond. Players come across the magnaron on What's Under There? or Xuk It!. As a world boss, Drov starts spawning the week of December 2, 2014 after the weekly maintenance. Either Drov or Tarlna the Ageless will spawn each week in Gorgrond.

Drowned Southsea Strongarms are humans located in Lost Rigger Cove in Tanaris.

Druids of the Fin are druids in sea lion form located in the Emerald Bay in Val'sharah. They are being lulled into a forced sleep by the Hypnotic Water Lilies, leaving them vulnerable to the nearby Bay Threshers.
Drowned Nightwatchers are night elves located in Nar'thalas Academy of Azsuna. They are fighting the Hatecoil naga.

Druids of the Branch are restoration druids located at Deliverance Point on the Broken Shore.
__NOTOC__ Drol'maz is a nathrezim located in Val'sharah during the Legion Assaults.
Drowning Warriors are orcs located around Legion's Fate and Seafarer's Tomb in Kelp'thar Forest. Some of them were unfortunate and drowned, while others were rescued.

Drowned Guardians are skeletons located in the Borean Tundra. They appear during Finding the Phylactery.

The Drunken Gryphon is a tavern located in Dampwick Ward in Boralus. Poor Vagrants can be found sitting in the sun on the balcony, while the tavern itself is the hangout for Dubious Guards as well as members of the Scrimshaw gang.
Druidic Touch is a Restoration druid artifact trait gained from G'Hanir, the Mother Tree. This is a hidden trait that does not appear in either your spellbook or the artifact traits pane.
The Drums of War trailer is the official trailer for Drums of War Patch 1.12.
__NOTOC__ The Drunken Drummer is located in the Zocalo in Dazar'alor. It is a known rest point, with many musical drums.

Drowned Sailors are skeletal corpses located at the Third Fleet shipwrecks in the Great Sea. They were human soldiers who fought during the Second War. As members of Kul Tiras they were part of the Third Fleet. They died during the Battle of Crestfall when red dragons breathed fire on their vessels, sending their ships to the bottom of the sea.

Most of them are rescued in Pay It Forward (Alliance) when encased into a bubble by the Enchanted Conch.

Drowned Kul Tiras Sailors are dead humans located in Durotar.

Droman Oulfarran is a tirnenn initially located in the Oaken Assembly in the Mists of Tirna Scithe. They have been enslaved by Ingra Maloch but when brought low they will break free and weaken Ingra Maloch for a time. Should the Drust interloper survive, they will once again enslave Droman Oulfarran. After the encounter, Droman Oulfarran will be seen at key points throughout the rest of the dungeon.

The Drowned Market is located in Nazjatar. It is here the refugees of Ara-Hinam arrived, and later that Queen Azshara tried to stop the tides engulfing down Zin-Azshari. A memory of the event still haunts the place.
Droman Tashmur is a tirnenn located at Tirna Vaal in Ardenweald.
Droolspine is a skeletal hound encountered by Class Order champions in Val'sharah.

Drowned Defias are dead humans, worgen, blood elves located in the Vision of Stormwind.
Droman is a title for some of the Ardenweald leaders, most of which belong to the Court of Night. The Droman's Hunting Horn can be used to summon the Wild Hunt.

Drippy is a dredger trainee who appears during Training Our Forces (Venthyr), Training in Ardenweald (Venthyr), Training in Bastion (Venthyr), and Training in Maldraxxus (Venthyr). He'll follow you and assist in combat while in the correct zone for the current training quest. He periodically offers an Extra Action Button spell, , which summons Big Chugas to assist you for 30 seconds. Additionally, every 5 minutes, a Dirty Glinting Object will spawn when you leave combat while Drippy is active. The object can contain a variety of goodies, including a companion pet: Lucy's Lost Collar. He can later be seen at the Vault of Secrets in Korthia, alongside Kashaa and Nandor.
Droman Aliothe's Best Friend is a level 60 Venthyr Covenant quest that becomes available after reaching Best Friend status with Droman Aliothe through the Ember Court.
Drithen the Boisterous is a vrykul located in the Great Mead Hall in Skyhold during A Hate-Hate Relationship. He is seen facing off against Halfdan Sly-Stalker, encircled by many Valarjar Aspirants.
Drunken Monkeys were hozen located on the Wandering Isle. While they use pygmy models, the quest text implies the model to be a placeholder.
Drogstitch Chestguard is a quest reward from Can't Hold a Candle To You.
Drim is a broker innkeeper located at Pilgrim's Grace in Zereth Mortis.
Drink Tray is found at the Grace of the Remembered in Bastion. It is part of the process to obtain the Memorial Offerings.

Dripping Fangs would have dropped from Boneweave Ambushers and Boneweave Rampagers near the House of Eyes in Maldraxxus.
Droman Fitia is a dryad. She could be slowed with the Vial of Caustic Goo.
Drunk Pirates are two humans located in a cave at Boralus Harbor in Tazavesh, the Veiled Market.

Drop It Like It's Hot is awarded to players who kill one of the three bosses of the Storm's Fury event in the Primalist Future of Thaldraszus. To gain stacks of Warmth, use a Field Deployable Heat Source (or stand in another player's). The heat source lasts for fifteen seconds and provides a stack per second.

Drowning Crewmen are humans, dwarves, and gnomes located in Kelp'thar Forest.

Druid and Priest Statue Set is a rare archaeology artifact that requires 150 skill to find and 100 Night Elf Archaeology Fragments to solve. Up to three Highborne Scroll keystones may be used to complete it.

Dueling is a way for players in the PvE environment to fight each other consensually. Players from opposite factions can duel, but the mechanism is primarily for dueling players of the same faction. Perfect for challenging friends or testing your skills against your peers 1 on 1, duels offer no rewards, save the sweet taste of victory.

Dryads are the enchanted daughters of the demigod Cenarius. The playful, frolicking creatures vaguely resemble a female night elf for the upper part of their bodies, while the lower part is more akin to woodland fawns. They are swift and sure and are at peace with all of the children of the forest. Like the keepers of the grove, while they prefer peace and abhor unnecessary violence, the dryads will defend the wildlands of Kalimdor with their lives if need be. They are curious, but only a few leave the forests. They can enter the Emerald Dream by shifting their bodies between the planes. Being the children of Cenarius, they have shared ancestry with the centaurs. Some are the children of Rem

Dun Baldar (or Dun'Baldar) is the stronghold of Alliance General Vanndar Stormpike, located in the northern part of Alterac Valley. Vanndar himself is in the keep on which the stronghold is built around. Dun Baldar is the primary staging ground for the Stormpike clan of dwarves, arriving in Alterac Valley in search of archaeological artifacts and resources. Encountering heavy resistance from the Frostwolf Clan, the Stormpike have received military aid from all members of the Alliance, seeking to drive out the Frostwolf and make the valley their own. Dun Baldar is close to the Alliance battleground entrance, allowing it to receive easy reinforcements from Alliance soldiers entering the battle
Drygulch Ravine is a location in Durotar. Apart from falling down into the ravine from above, the only entrance is from Razorwind Canyon, through a small cave at .

Duke Lionheart was a paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand who accompanied the Human Expedition to Kalimdor during the Third War. Following Mannoroth's death, Jaina Proudmoore and Thrall put Lionheart in charge of a joint orc and human base in Ashenvale in order to hunt the remaining demons. Lionheart upheld orderly conduct between the humans and orcs, who often argued with each other. He didn't seem to mind working with the orcs, unlike some of his men. Tyrande Whisperwind and the Sentinels watched them from the nearby woods and eventually killed the paladin as punishment for intruding on the forest.

Dun Garok was a dwarven keep nestled into the southeastern hills of Hillsbrad Foothills. Led by Captain Ironhill, the dwarves helped protect the humans of Hillsbrad as well as the Azurelode Mine. The Forsaken loathed the presence of these dwarves and once offered several quests for Horde adventurers to infiltrate Dun Garok and kill the dwarves within. The Forsaken, outnumbering the dwarves ten-to-one, assaulted them with all their might. The dwarves fought until the bitter end, but every last one of them died in defense of Dun Garok. Dun Niffelem is a fortress of massive spikes of ice and iron chains, spreading out to block off an entire section of the Valley of Ancient Winters, in the eastern of Storm Peaks. It is home to the Sons of Hodir, a clan of frost giants, and their ruler King Jokkum.

Duchess Mynx is the quartermaster of the Knights of the Ebon Blade and is located in the Shadow Vault in Icecrown. She can only be accessed after the Shadow Vault is controlled by the Knights of the Ebon Blade following completion of The Shadow Vault (quest). Mynx also appears in Keeper's Respite in Korthia, serving as the Death's Advance faction quartermaster.
The Dual-Plagued Brain was used in the Scourge Invasion quests. While held it whispered the adventurer, alternating between the zombie language and one the adventurer could understand.

Dubra'Jin is a small Zandalari outpost that is located west of Gundrak in Zul'Drak. It is also the name of the forgotten god, represented by the nearby statue. By sacrificing raptor eggs to the god, he, in turn, protects the few trolls there from being overrun by the Drakkari.

This is a list of all the Dude, Where's My Mount? Episodes. *Note that these contain the complete storyline of every episode.

Dude, Where's My Mount? was a machinima created by Apt-T Productions. The theme tune to the beginning title was Butthole Surfers - Dracula From Houston, but was changed in episode 8. The show started running all the way back in 2004 when the first episode was made and left for about a year. Then the team thought of making more episodes and soon, they were offered to join Machinima Inc. and have been part of the machinima community since 2007. After the shutdown of Machinima Inc in Febuary 2019, the fate of the series remains unknown, though they retained publishing rights and reuploaded the first season to their YouTube channel.

=== Design Goals === * Have a realistically low level of bookkeeping. * Not penalize fill-ins or first-time raiders. * Give people some control over whether they get loot in a given week or not. * Never give loot to off-spec raiders or shard loot that is of benefit to main specs. * Work well in a raiding syndicate comprised of multiple guilds and individuals. * Allow alts to gain gear on "farm bosses," but not at the expense of mains. ----

Dumass is a Forsaken quest giver initially found at the Southpoint Gate for the quest Welcome to the Machine, where the player sends him on an adventure. He later shows up in the Azurelode Mine where he's fallen victim to the spiders there. After being rescued, Captain Keyton asks the rescuer if they have heard of "survival of the fittest". Keyton then orders Dumass to travel to Tarren Mill, though Dumass seems to believe it is found somewhere in the Barrens. His whereabouts after this is unknown. His dialogue indicates that Dumass suffered the most extreme side effect (being stripped of any and all rational thought) that can happen from being resurrected by the Val'kyr.

The Drysnout are a group of gnolls inhabiting the Badlands making up 40% of the area's population. They are more numerous than the other factions, due mainly to the fact that their birth rate is higher than that of randy rabbits. The gnolls are easy prey for the Dark Iron dwarves, drakes and ogres that roam the Badlands. You can tell a Drysnout because he wears brown clothing, simple leather armor, and is running for his life.

The Drustvar Militia was a league of humans who fought and defeated the Drust. The Drustvar Militia formed when the Drust started attacking newly constructed human settlements. Even though the humans tried to live in peace with the Drust, it was clear that war was unavoidable. Led by their leader Gorak Tul, the Drust pushed the humans back from every settlement they made. With the only viable option of retreat left, Drustvar Militia hired several scholars to see what could be done about the Drust. The Dueler's Guild is a new Player vs Player feature introduced in Battle for Azeroth. With War Mode enabled, players at level 120 can speak with a NPC (respectively Bouncers for the Alliance and Troll Guards for the Horde) who will queue them to take part in 1-on-1 duels at Hook Point of Boralus or Mugambala of Zuldazar. Once in the arena, you'll battle it out against a rival player to see who continues on. If you lose, you're out. Getting far enough through the gauntlet of players will provide some achievements, including Master of Duels, which rewards the title Contender.
